conclusion_quantitative: unknown (Ask) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 2 autonomy limits, 5 clarification rules, 7 approval gates, 10+ validation rules; none for escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: This skill (no name given; the file is named by its hash) is a brainstorming workflow that turns a vague request into an approved, written design before any plan or code. Its central rule is a hard gate: no implementation action until the user approves the design, section by section and then as a written spec. The agent asks one question at a time and proposes alternatives, self-reviews the spec, and confirms everything with a checklist. It hands off only to the planner and sets no rules for handling failure.

statements.quote: Do NOT invoke the implementer directly.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 5 clarification rules (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 5 rules, all strict, 1 tied to a situation, all bullet points. The agent asks clarifying questions about purpose, constraints and success criteria one at a time, preferably multiple choice and never bundled. It proposes 2 to 3 approaches with trade-offs and its recommendation rather than a single option, and goes back to clarify whenever something does not make sense.

statements.quote: **Ask clarifying questions, one at a time** — purpose, constraints, success criteria. Prefer multiple choice. Never bundle multiple questions in one message.
**Propose 2-3 approaches with trade-offs** — lead with your recommendation and why. Do not present a single option as the only way.
**One question at a time** — never overwhelm with a batch.
**Multiple choice preferred** — easier to answer than open-ended.
**Be flexible** — go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 7 approval gates (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list.

It asks for approval after each design section, asks the user to review the written spec, and hands off to the planner only once the user approves.
